compiled_state.description:
## Context
Dependabot PR **#131** ("deps: bump the uv-lock group with 5 updates", branch
`dependabot/uv/uv-lock-4320b5f53c`, opened 2026-08-19) is open and CANNOT be merged where it sits.
GitHub is a read-only mirror that rejects direct pushes and PR merges; every change to `main` flows
through Gerrit. So a dependabot PR only lands if someone re-authors it as a Gerrit change.

Precedent: `woodblock-gnatty-xiaosaurus` (5a90-ec98-af5a-48d0) did exactly this for PRs #129/#130 via
Gerrit change 1832, merged 2026-08-17. Dependabot then auto-closed both PRs when the mirror picked
up the landed commit. Expect the same mechanism here — but see AC5: it must be VERIFIED, not assumed.

## What the PR changes
Two files:
- `pyproject.toml` — one line: `"ruff==0.16.2"` -> `"ruff==0.16.3"`
- `uv.lock` — +81/-73

Five package updates:

| package | from | to |
|---|---|---|
| `botocore` | 1.43.70 | 1.43.72 |
| `genai-prices` | 0.1.2 | 0.1.3 |
| `json-repair` | 0.63.1 | 0.63.2 |
| `mypy` | 2.3.0 | 2.3.1 |
| `ruff` | 0.16.2 | 0.16.3 |

## This is NOT a pure lockfile bump — read this before planning
`mypy` and `ruff` ARE the typecheck and lint gates. Bumping them can surface findings the previous
versions did not report, anywhere in the tree, in code this ticket did not otherwise touch. That is
the substance of the work, not an obstacle to it:

- New findings must be FIXED, not suppressed. Do not add `# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, or per-rule
  exclusions to make a new gate version quiet — that converts a tool upgrade into hidden debt and
  defeats the reason for upgrading.
- If a new rule is genuinely unwanted for this project, that is a DELIBERATE configuration decision
  and belongs in its own ticket with its rationale, not smuggled in beside a version bump.
- If the fallout is large enough to dominate the change, STOP and report rather than absorbing it.
  Splitting "bump the tools" from "fix what the new tools found" into stacked changes is the correct
  response to a big blast radius, and is cheaper than one unreviewable change.
- The complexity ratchet (`scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py`) is shrink-only. A newer ruff may
  score an unchanged function differently; if that trips the ratchet, fix by behaviour-preserving
  extraction, NEVER by editing `.github/complexity-baseline.json` (`--lock`/`--update-stale` are
  maintenance-only, not a contributor escape hatch).

## Verify before acting
Dependabot may supersede #131 with a newer grouped PR before this ticket is worked. Re-check
`gh pr view 131 --repo navapbc/rebar` first. If it is closed or superseded, do NOT re-apply stale
pins — record the finding and close this ticket as superseded, naming the PR that replaced it.
Re-pinning versions that a later PR has already moved past actively fights dependabot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] PR #131 is confirmed still open and current at the time work begins; if superseded, this
      ticket is closed as superseded naming the replacement PR, and no code change is made.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` pins `ruff==0.16.3`, and `uv.lock` records botocore 1.43.72,
      genai-prices 0.1.3, json-repair 0.63.2, mypy 2.3.1 and ruff 0.16.3. The lock is regenerated
      with the project's own uv workflow, not hand-edited.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass under the NEW ruff and mypy. Any newly-surfaced finding
      is fixed in the code; no `# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, or rule exclusion is added to silence
      one. The complexity baseline file is unmodified.
- [ ] **The change LANDS**: pushed to Gerrit, `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1` with no unresolved
      comments, submitted, and merged to `main`. The ticket records the change number and the
      merged commit sha.
- [ ] **PR #131 is CLOSED**: verified closed after the merge via
      `gh pr view 131 --repo navapbc/rebar --json state`. If dependabot has not auto-closed it
      within a reasonable window after the mirror syncs, close it manually with a comment naming
      the Gerrit change and merged commit that superseded it. Do not leave it open on the
      assumption that automation will get to it.

## Testing
`make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite must pass on the new pins. Because the bump
touches the lint and typecheck tools, a green run is the evidence that the upgrade is complete —
not merely that the lockfile parses.

file_impact.reason: Bump the ruff pin from 0.16.2 to 0.16.3.
Regenerate the lock for botocore, genai-prices, json-repair, mypy and ruff.
